title: The integral coefficient inclusion is the unique ring map over E_X -> F_X.
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, fix an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with its extending absolute value, and let $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$ be finite subextensions, with their restricted absolute values and topologies [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring]. Write $\mathcal O_H=\{x\in H:|x|\le1\}$ with its subspace topology, for $H=E,F$, and $\underline{\mathcal O_H}(S)=C(S,\mathcal O_H)$ for its condensed ring [def-sfb-padic-integers-condensed-ring]. Let $X$ be any scheme, using the small pro-étale site and universes of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Put $\mathcal O_{H,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_H}$ and $H_X=p_X^*\underline H$, with the transported ring-object structures [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $a_{H,X}:\mathcal O_{H,X}\to H_X$ be the canonical integral inclusion [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield], and let $i_{E,F,X}:E_X\to F_X$ be the coefficient map induced by the specified field inclusion [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map]. There exists exactly one morphism $\varphi:\mathcal O_{E,X}\to\mathcal O_{F,X}$ of underlying abelian sheaves such that it preserves the unit and multiplication of these ring objects and
$$a_{F,X}\circ\varphi=i_{E,F,X}\circ a_{E,X}.$$
Here preservation of the ring-object structure is the Lean predicate $\mathrm{IsMonHom}(\varphi)$, not the categorical monomorphism predicate.

proof.text: Let $j:E\hookrightarrow F$ be the given inclusion. By [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring], both absolute values are restrictions of the same value on $\Omega$, so $|j(x)|_F=|x|_E$. By [def-sfb-padic-integers-condensed-ring], membership in either integer ring is precisely the inequality $|x|\le1$. Thus $r:\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_F$, $x\mapsto j(x)$, is well defined and preserves all ring operations. For $x,y\in\mathcal O_E$, $|r(x)-r(y)|_F=|x-y|_E$, so it is continuous in the specified subspace topologies. The ordinary inclusions $a_H:\mathcal O_H\hookrightarrow H$ satisfy $a_F\circ r=j\circ a_E$ by evaluation at each $x$.

source.place: Integral coefficients and inclusions in the colimit over finite subextensions; explicit restriction argument in the attached Lean docstring

proof.text: Apply [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map] to $r$. This gives a ring-object morphism $b:\underline{\mathcal O_E}\to\underline{\mathcal O_F}$ whose component at a profinite set $S$ sends $f$ to $r\circ f$. The integral inclusion $a_H$ induces the postcomposition map $\underline a_H$ of [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield-point], and the field map induces $\underline j$ of [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-map]. Both composites in $\underline a_F\circ b=\underline j\circ\underline a_E$ send $f$ to the identical function $S\to F$, so they are equal as natural transformations.

source.place: Postcomposition construction and its strict functoriality

proof.text: Use the functor on ring objects of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and put $\varphi=p_X^*b$. It preserves unit and multiplication. Functoriality applied to the equality of step 2 gives $p_X^*(\underline a_F)\circ\varphi=p_X^*(\underline j)\circ p_X^*(\underline a_E)$. By [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield], $p_X^*(\underline a_H)=a_{H,X}$ for $H=E,F$. By [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map], $i_{E,F,X}$ is the coefficient change of $\underline j$, which by [def-sfb-coefficient-map] is $p_X^*(\underline j)$. So these three maps are exactly $a_{F,X}$, $i_{E,F,X}$ and $a_{E,X}$, respectively. This proves existence with the required square and the specified coefficient objects.

source.place: Applying the monoidal coefficient functor; parent integral-twist paragraph

proof.text: The point functor $u:S\mapsto\operatorname{Spec}LC(S,\mathbf Z)$ preserves finite limits and coverings and is continuous by clause 1 of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. Profinite sets have the point as terminal object and fibre products with their usual subspace topology (closed subspaces of finite products of compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces); hence they have finite limits. Work in a common larger sheaf universe, as in that node. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] to $u$: the sheafified Kan-extension functor $p^*$ preserves finite limits on abelian sheaves. The functor $\pi_X^*$ for $\pi_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ preserves finite limits by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-exact]. Clause 4 of the first node identifies $p_X^*=\pi_X^*\circ p^*$. A composite of these two functors therefore preserves finite limits: its comparison maps are composites of the two invertible finite-limit comparisons.

source.place: Tag 00X6, proposition-get-morphism; applied to the blueprint point functor and composed with the scheme inverse image

proof.text: The map $\underline a_F$ of step 2 is a categorical monomorphism. Indeed if $v,w:G\to\underline{\mathcal O_F}$ have equal composites with it, then for every profinite $S$ and $z\in G(S)$ the functions $v_S(z)$ and $w_S(z)$ have the same values in $F$. Injectivity of the subset inclusion $\mathcal O_F\hookrightarrow F$ makes them equal in $\mathcal O_F$, so $v=w$. A map $m:A\to B$ is monic exactly when its square with both parallel sides $m$ and both other sides $\mathrm{id}_A$ is a pullback: the pullback universal property is precisely cancellation of $m$. The finite-limit preservation in step 4 sends this square for $\underline a_F$ to that square for $p_X^*\underline a_F=a_{F,X}$. Thus $a_{F,X}$ is monic as an underlying abelian-sheaf morphism.

source.place: Section formula for the inclusion; elementary cancellation and pullback characterization of a monomorphism

proof.text: If $\psi$ is another ring-object morphism satisfying the prescribed square, then $a_{F,X}\circ\psi=i_{E,F,X}\circ a_{E,X}=a_{F,X}\circ\varphi$. By the cancellation proved in step 5, $\psi=\varphi$. This is uniqueness of the underlying morphism, and the property of preserving unit and multiplication contributes no additional choice.

theorem spIntegersMap_existsUnique {E F : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ}
    (h : E ≤ F) :
    ∃! φ : condensedRingObj.{u} (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj.{u} ℓ E.1) X ⟶
        condensedRingObj.{u} (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj.{u} ℓ F.1) X,
      IsMonHom φ ∧
      φ ≫ padicIntegersToPadicSubfield X ℓ F =
        padicIntegersToPadicSubfield X ℓ E ≫
          coefficientMap.{u} (Profinite.padicSubfieldRingObjMap ℓ h) X := by
  sorry
